items.title: Iran says US is blocking Hormuz deal as Oman talks near terms
items.summary: Tehran's Revolutionary Guard says Iran and Oman have agreed terms for safe transit but the strait stays closed until Washington accepts Iranian conditions; only about five commercial vessels transited on the day.

items.title: جست‌وجوی زندهٔ «تنگه هرمز» در گوگل‌نیوز
items.summary: نقطهٔ ورود تجمیعی به آخرین اخبار فارسی دربارهٔ تنگهٔ هرمز؛ اعتبار پایین چون منبعِ منفرد ندارد و راستی‌آزمایی نشده است.

items.title: بحث حيّ عن «مضيق هرمز» في غوغل نيوز
items.summary: نقطة دخول تجميعية لأحدث الأخبار العربية عن مضيق هرمز؛ الثقة منخفضة لأنه مُجمِّع وليس مصدراً منفرداً، وغير مُتحقَّق.

items.title: Reddit search: public posts mentioning Hormuz
items.summary: User-generated posts and discussion threads referencing the strait; lowest confidence tier, unverified social chatter.

items.title: Tracking data shows how many ships still defy the Hormuz risk
items.summary: Analysis of transit data shows the waterway split into a northern Iranian route and a southern Omani route, with daily crossings far below the pre-war average.

items.title: Ships face a perilous path through the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Live coverage reports continued standoff between Washington and Tehran over control of the waterway, with shipping disruptions compounded by Red Sea attacks.

items.title: IEA calls Hormuz closure the largest oil-supply disruption on record
items.summary: The August Oil Market Report cuts 2026 supply and demand forecasts, citing continued closure of the strait and renewed maritime attacks.

items.title: EIA: Hormuz oil transit fell to about 4.9 million b/d in Q2 2026
items.summary: Short-Term Energy Outlook estimates crude and liquids through the strait dropped sharply from roughly 21.6 million b/d before the conflict, with prices easing if traffic recovers.

items.title: Iran sets sweeping conditions to reopen Hormuz after tanker hit
items.summary: Tehran demands the US lift its naval blockade and sanctions, withdraw regional forces and pay reparations before reopening; a UAE-operated vessel was reportedly struck.

items.title: CRS: prolonged instability in the Strait of Hormuz could persist
items.summary: Congressional Research Service reviews security developments and market impacts, noting the status quo may hold as long as both sides bear the cost.

items.title: US, Iran and Oman near an interim deal to reopen Hormuz
items.summary: Sources describe a proposed 60-day temporary arrangement between Oman and Iran, brokered with Qatari, Pakistani and Saudi mediation, aimed at restoring the ceasefire.

items.title: Crisis Group flags Hormuz threat level as critical
items.summary: The watchlist entry tracks Iran-Oman talks and warns an intentional or inadvertent incident at sea could escalate quickly.
